committee: CC Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee
overview: The CC Resident Services and Public Engagement Committee is a subcommittee of the Medford City Council tasked with public outreach, council communication, civic education, and reviewing municipal service policies. The committee met 23 times in the archive between May 15, 2024 and October 7, 2026. Over this span, the committee regularly edited and authorized the City Council newsletter, organized constituent listening sessions, and reviewed municipal policy measures such as veteran housing incentives, human rights ordinances, and budget feedback surveys. As of the October 7, 2026 meeting, the committee is active in executing a schedule of neighborhood ward meetings, drafting updates to the city's noise ordinance, evaluating city website accessibility, and maintaining the council newsletter workflow.

threads.name: City Council Newsletter
threads.summary: The committee regularly drafts, edits, and approves monthly and quarterly updates summarizing City Council resolutions, meetings, and public notices (M02#2, M04#1, M16#1). Throughout the 2024-2025 term, members refined newsletter content to maintain neutral tone, highlight legislative accomplishments, and include links to municipal boards (M02#2, M07#2, M12#1). In 2026, the committee implemented a rotating schedule assigning individual councilors to author upcoming monthly editions (M18#1, M21#2). At the October 2026 meeting, the committee considered a resolution allowing direct approval and distribution of newsletters without requiring full City Council referral (M23#1).

threads.name: Community Listening Sessions and Ward Meetings
threads.summary: In May 2024, the committee initiated plans for public listening sessions targeting diverse demographic groups across Medford (M01#2, M06#3). Sessions held at local venues like the Senior Center yielded resident feedback on roads, housing, and navigating municipal contact information (M09#2, M12#3, M15#2). In 2026, the committee expanded this format into a structured strategy to hold hybrid neighborhood meetings across all eight city wards (M17#3, M18#2, M21#3). Following the inaugural Ward 1 meeting in September 2026, the committee finalized a schedule extending remaining ward meetings into early 2027 (M23#2).

threads.name: Human Rights Commission Modernization
threads.summary: In October 2024, the committee received an update that a draft Human Rights Commission ordinance was under administrative review by the Mayor and Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Director (M05#2). In early 2025, members reviewed proposed ordinance revisions covering membership size, officer roles, stipends, and meeting frequency (M09#1, M10#2). In May 2025, the committee approved amendments fixing commission membership at 11 individuals, authorizing a $1,250 annual stipend, and clarifying removal procedures (M13#1). The committee then voted to refer the modernized draft ordinance to the full City Council (M13#1).

threads.name: Municipal Budget Public Engagement
threads.summary: The committee initiated a public engagement plan in April 2025 to collect resident feedback regarding the upcoming FY 2026 municipal budget (M10#3). Members reviewed and amended a public survey to include budget graphics, demographic questions, and preferred outreach channels (M11#1, M13#3). Survey responses gathered input from over 100 residents identifying schools and infrastructure as primary short-term priorities (M12#2, M14#2). The formal survey report was distributed to the full City Council and placed on file in June 2025 (M14#2).

threads.name: Veteran Housing Incentive Program
threads.summary: In May 2024, the Director of Veterans' Services presented a pilot program proposal offering annual stipends to landlords who rent to qualified veterans (M02#1). The committee voted to send the proposal to legal counsel while keeping the paper in committee (M02#1). In November 2024, the committee refined the proposal into a pilot program providing $750 annual rebates to owner-occupant landlords, administered through Housing Families using Veteran Services Office funds (M06#1). The committee then referred the proposal to legal counsel and the full City Council (M06#1).

threads.name: Noise Ordinance Update
threads.summary: The committee scheduled a initial discussion to revise the city's 1974 noise ordinance in August 2026 (M21#4). In September 2026, members reviewed regulatory models from peer municipalities and discussed enforcement challenges with existing rules (M22#3). A draft ordinance modeled on Somerville's policy was presented in October 2026, introducing measurable decibel limits, a list of 17 defined disturbances, and a non-criminal fine structure (M23#3). The item was kept in committee to allow for a public survey and consultations with local businesses and the police department (M23#3).

threads.name: Resident Procedural Guide and Website Improvements
threads.summary: In June 2024, the committee authorized the creation of a resident procedural guide to clarify City Council meeting processes and public comment options (M03#2). After editing terms and speaking guidelines, the committee referred the completed procedural guide to the full City Council in September 2024 (M04#2). In October 2026, the committee shifted focus to digital communication channels by reviewing an audit of the city website detailing broken links and accessibility issues (M23#4). The committee kept the website improvement plan in committee to plan a joint meeting with the IT and Communications departments (M23#4).
